- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; apply downward correction of 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates downside risk; increase forecast margin for downside protection.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, forecast remains high for 2–3 periods; adjust by adding 1–2% downward bias for lagged sentiment.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; if recent 5–7 day range is tight, apply slight upward bias to avoid underestimating volatility.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent trend; use 3-period moving average of sentiment to smooth and adjust forecast direction.
